issues.failure_explanation: The prose says the penultimate limit for Omega^alpha is contained in the spectrum up to error, and calls this Sigma_2. The displayed guarantee is the opposite: the spectrum is contained in the limit plus a ball, i.e. covering, which the appendix classifies as Pi_2. The Omega^m case is described with the reverse swap. So the advertised one-sided verification guarantees are misattributed.

failure_location.quote: The penultimate limit in \cref{Sigma_example} is \textit{contained in} the desired set, up to a controllable error.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the Sigma_2/Pi_2 descriptions so that they match the displayed inclusions and the appendix classifications.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are told the wrong direction of error control (which kind of verification is available) for each class.
issues.title: Sigma_2/Pi_2 verification labels swapped for the two-limit towers
issues.why_classification: A local relabelling makes the prose consistent with the proved results, and no mathematical content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Omega_X^m is defined only by measure preservation and allows discontinuous F, so the inclusion Omega_X^m ⊂ Omega_X (continuous maps) is false. The Sigma_2 claim for Omega_X^m is then contradicted by the paper's own thm:rotation(c). That result shows that discontinuous measure-preserving invertible circle maps, which have unitary Koopman operators with spectrum equal to Sp_ap, have infinite SCI.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add continuity (and non-singularity/boundedness) to the definition of Omega_X^m, as the main-text setup already assumes.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the Omega_X^m classifications are false. They hold only for continuous measure-preserving maps.
issues.title: Omega_X^m omits continuity, contradicting Theorem thm:rotation(c)
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local hypothesis that the advertised setting already assumes, and the method and conclusion survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in Omega^delta also requires (F^{-1})' ≤ 1+delta. At the r_1→r_2 junction this derivative is (1-r_1)/(r_1(1-r_2)). Under deriv_bound this is only bounded by (1+delta)^2, because both factors may be close to 1+delta. Hence the claim that F_{c^{(k)}} lies in Omega^delta is unproved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen deriv_bound to also require (1-r_1)/(r_1(1-r_2)) ≤ 1+delta. This is achievable with r_1<r_2 near 1 and (1-r_1)/(1-r_2) slightly above 1, with tau taken small.
issues.overall_effect: Membership of the adversarial maps (including the limit F_c) in Omega^delta is not established, so the lower bound is not justified as written.
issues.title: Inverse-derivative bound at junctions not ensured in interval construction
issues.why_classification: A short adjustment of the parameter constraints restores the argument with the same statement.

issues.failure_explanation: For F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x)), every function g(x) of x alone satisfies K_F g = g. For example cos(x) is a non-constant eigenfunction in span{1}^⊥, so part (a) is false. The claimed C^0 conjugacy to (x,y+x) is also impossible, because the symmetric f is not injective. Hence Xi_p^dec equals 1 for every map in the construction. The alternation 0/1 used to prove that Xi_p^dec is not in Delta_2^P collapses. The Sp_pp lower bound survives, since there the eigenvalue set is still {1}.

failure_location.quote: It follows that there are no eigenfunctions in the subspace $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct an adversarial family of ergodic maps in Omega_p that alternate between weakly mixing and having non-trivial eigenvalues, or else change the decision problem to eigenvalues different from 1.
issues.overall_effect: The impossibility of deciding existence of non-trivial eigenfunctions (weak mixing) in one limit is unproven. This is a headline claim of thm4/thm:torus.
